column1: # *** ARTIGAS - THE DEPARTMENT NOBODY HAD OPENED. 12 October 2026. ***
# Artigas sits on the Brazilian border, 500km north of everything this archive has worked. It
# appeared here for the first time this morning, when a cross-spelling sweep turned up a birth act
# at San Eugenio and the plate gave a Lerena household nobody had met.
# *** THIS FILE IS A SURVEY, NOT A READING. *** Every row below is from the RECORD INDEX. One act
# has been opened at the plate - act 110 of 2 June 1899 - and it is recorded in
# data/variant-parent-sweep.tsv. Nothing here is tiered and no line is joined to this family's.
*** A DEPARTMENT THIS ARCHIVE HAD NEVER OPENED ***
column2: record index, each of eight spellings exact, q.anyPlace = Artigas, Uruguay
column3: *** THE COUNTS PUBLISHED HERE THIS AFTERNOON WERE WRONG AND ARE WITHDRAWN. ***
column4: Artigas, on the Brazilian border, appears nowhere in this archive's searched list. Everything here assumes the family runs Canelones to Montevideo to Trinidad.
column5: *** q.anyPlace FALLS BACK TO THE COUNTRY. *** 'Nonesuch, Uruguay' - a department that does not exist - returns 1,787, the whole-country figure; and records indexed only to 'Uruguay', or to no place at all, satisfy every departmental query. *** Of the first hundred hits, 15 name Artigas, 28 name somewhere else entirely, and 57 carry no place in the index. *** So '208 against 699 for Flores' compared two inflated numbers and meant nothing. *** The honest statement is that Artigas is a department this archive has never worked and that a Lerena family demonstrably lived there - which is still true, and is still worth a session. *** See data/corrections.tsv, 12 October.

column1: *** AND IT DOES NOT ANSWER THE CENTRAL QUESTION ***
column2: Juan Carlos exact as subject and as father, and Lerena father x Lerena mother, all inside Artigas
column4: The department was opened because it was unworked, not because anything pointed a Juan Carlos at it.
column5: *** No Juan Carlos Lerena at Artigas in any role, and no Lerena-Lerena couple there. *** *** AND THESE NULLS SURVIVE THE CORRECTION ABOVE, because a filter that WIDENS cannot hide a record - if anything it should have returned MORE. *** A null from an over-wide query is stronger than a null from a tight one, which is the one piece of luck in this row.

column1: *** BENITO LERENA'S HOUSEHOLD, AND WHAT IT COST HIM ***
column2: the 208, read for the man found on act 110 of 1899
column3: *** FIVE INFANT DEATHS REGISTERED AT ARTIGAS BETWEEN 1893 AND 1902 ***
column4: Benito Lerena was found this morning as the declarant on his grandson's birth act - 45 years old, a jornalero who could not sign his name.
column5: An unnamed child *** Lerena, died 6 November 1893 ***; another *** died 8 November 1894 ***; *** IDERSIO LERENA ARAUJO, died 19 December 1896 ***; *** GUMERSINDO LERENA, born 1898, died 8 March 1899 ***; and another *** died 25 July 1902. *** Gumersindo died ten weeks before Benito walked into the Juzgado de Paz to register his daughter's son. *** Index-level, every one: no act has been opened. ***

column1: *** THE MOTHER THE INDEX COULD NOT NAME ***
column2: the same five deaths, read for the mother's surname
column3: *** ARAUJO, CORDERO, CUESTIMA, ARAUJO CARDOZO - and 'Maria Cristina' with no surname at all ***
column4: The act of 1899, read at the plate this morning, calls her *** Dona Maria Cristina, 43, brasilera *** and gives her NO SURNAME. That is how the act is written.
column5: *** FOUR DIFFERENT SURNAMES FOR ONE WOMAN, IN ONE DEPARTMENT, IN NINE YEARS - because the record keeps handing the indexer a woman with one name and the index has a field that must be filled. *** ARAUJO is the likeliest reading: it appears twice, and once as Araujo Cardozo. *** This is the mother-manufacturing failure this archive already documented, caught in the open and five times over. ***

column1: *** ANASTASIA'S SECOND SON, EIGHT YEARS ON ***
column3: *** TEODORO ALVES LERENA, born 22 April 1907, registered 30 April 1907 at Artigas ***
column4: Act 110 of 1899 gave Anastasia Lerena, 22, married to the Brazilian soldier Honorio Alvarez, with one son - Juan Ildebel.
column5: *** The same couple, eight years later, under the spelling ALVES rather than ALVAREZ. *** So Juan Ildebel and Teodoro are brothers, and the marriage lasted. A third child, *** Crisena Alves ***, is indexed to Honorio with a birth year of 1816 - which in this collection means the year was not read.

column1: *** AND TWO MORE LERENA LINES - BUT NOT AT ARTIGAS ***
column3: *** DOMINGO LERENA and PEDRO A. LERENA ***
column4: Nothing. Neither name is in this register.
column5: *** DOMINGO LERENA *** with a wife indexed *** Maria Cristina Araujo *** - the same wife-name as Benito's, so either a brother, or one man under two names, or the index conflating two households. Their daughter *** ASUNCION LERENA, b.1884 ***, later at San Francisco de Asis in Montevideo. *** NEITHER IS PLACED AT ARTIGAS: *** the index gives Asuncion's birth as 'Uruguay' with no department, and she reached this row only through the over-wide place filter corrected above. *** And PEDRO A. LERENA, who died 6 November 1896 aged 69, is a MONTEVIDEO death - the volume is 'Montevideo. Death Records 1896' - not an Artigas one. *** His spouse is given as *** MANUELA LEMOS ***, and a second death, of a Pedro Antonio Lerena born 1875, names the same Manuela as his mother. *** Three generations of the name, and the city is Montevideo. ***
